chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who fabricated [a charge of adultery] upon a group of people. He said: If they come with it [the charge] collectively, he is whipped with one Hadd (penalty); and if they come with it separately, a Hadd is inflicted upon each one of them.

key_terms.افْتَرَى: Fabricated a false charge (specifically of adultery/Li'an context)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in punishment for false accusation when a group accuses collectively versus separately?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the procedural nuance in the Hadd of Qadhf (false accusation of adultery), distinguishing between a unified legal action when accusers appear jointly versus individual liabilities when they testify separately. It reflects the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the precise mechanics of witness testimony and the prevention of double jeopardy or fragmented penalties in criminal law. The distinction ensures that the punishment aligns with the actual number of distinct accusations presented to the court.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who fabricated upon a group of people.
Heasws said: ‘If they come with it altogether, he would be whipped with one Penalty (Hadd), and if they come to be separately, he would be whipped a Penalty (Hadd) for each one of them’.
